data.narrative:
C12 Quantum Electronics is a Series A quantum computing company founded by Matthieu and Pierre Desjardins. The target operates within a 11-company comp universe consisting of 3 public peers (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and 8 private firms including Quantinuum, IonQ, PsiQuantum, D-Wave Quantum, and SandboxAQ.

Valuation analysis relies on a single applicable method. Stage-Progression applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier to the $19.4M total raised proxy, yielding an implied valuation of $39M. This multiplier reflects typical Series A to subsequent-stage progression dynamics. The Peer-Median method is not applicable due to insufficient granular peer coverage—while 8 quantum computing private companies exist in the broader dataset, zero same-stage, zero adjacent-stage, and zero similar-valuation-tier comparables survived filtering. Relying on an all-sector median would introduce unacceptable noise.

The single-method triangulation produces a range of $33M (low) to $45M (high), with a median point of $39M. The low and high bounds incorporate ±15% sensitivity around the stage-progression result. Given dependence on a single method and the thinness of near-peer comparables, the analysis is materially constrained by data availability. Key uncertainties include (1) the appropriateness of a 2.0x multiplier for this specific subsector and capital trajectory, and (2) whether public quantum computing comps meaningfully anchor private Series A valuation. Validation through additional tranches of institutional financing or expanded comparable datasets would strengthen confidence in this range.
